competences: The learner identify the condition and main clause.
The learner punctuate given if-sentences correctly.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and uses correctly: if, condition, main clause, present simple, future simple.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify the condition and main clause.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to punctuate given if-sentences correctly.
priorKnowledge: Learners can read simple sentences and recognise present and future actions.
materials: Chart showing an if-clause and a main clause

steps.content: Learners can read simple sentences and recognise present and future actions. Key words: if, condition, main clause, present simple, future simple
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays conditional-clause sentence cards and links the chart to the prior knowledge: Learners can read simple sentences and recognise present and future actions. The teacher pronounces the lesson vocabulary, checks learners’ reading, and introduces using if.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall familiar words, read the displayed key words aloud, and explain what they already know about the topic.

source.quote: We commonly use a future simple tense in the main clause

steps.content: Conditional clauses: If and unless introduce a conditional clause. The if-clause expresses a condition. The main clause commonly uses the future simple tense. The if-clause commonly uses the present simple tense.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: If and unless introduce a conditional clause. The if-clause expresses a condition. The main clause commonly uses the future simple tense. The if-clause commonly uses the present simple tense. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Punctuate: if i pass exams i will fly to london" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

steps.content: Punctuation: A comma follows the if-clause when it comes first.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: A comma follows the if-clause when it comes first. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Punctuate: if i get money i will buy a new radio" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: put a comma if the “if” clause comes first

steps.content: Example 1: If I get money, I will buy a new radio. If-clause: If I get money. Main clause: I will buy a new radio.

The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Read and write correctly: mother will punish us if we don’t complete the work" Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
